title: Spectral coefficient estimate for a finite map of affinoids
statement: Let $K$ be a complete field [def-weil-field] with a nontrivial real-valued nonarchimedean absolute value. Let $B,A$ be nonzero affinoid $K$-algebras, that is, quotients of restricted-series rings in finitely many variables [def-trf-restricted-series-presentation]. Let $\varphi:B\to A$ be a $K$-algebra homomorphism making $A$ a finitely generated $B$-module. For $H=A,B$ define $\rho_H(h)=\sup_{\mathfrak m\in\operatorname{Max}H}|h\bmod\mathfrak m|$, using the unique extensions of the absolute value to the finite residue fields, as in [lem-trf-affinoid-supremum-seminorm-calculus]. For every $a\in A$ there exist an integer $n\ge1$ and coefficients $b_1,\ldots,b_n\in B$ such that $a^n+\sum_{i=1}^n\varphi(b_i)a^{n-i}=0$ and $\rho_A(a)=\max_{1\le i\le n}\rho_B(b_i)^{1/i}$. Neither injectivity of $\varphi$ nor reducedness of either algebra is assumed.

source.place: Section 1.4, Lemma 13, printed pp.27-28, including its minimal-prime reduction and nilpotent-power argument. Primary PDF read online 2026-10-24; archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Write $\sigma_H(Z^e+\sum_{i=1}^e h_iZ^{e-i})=\max_i\rho_H(h_i)^{1/i}$ for $e\ge1$. The residue-field definition gives $\rho_H(x+y)\le\max(\rho_H(x),\rho_H(y))$, $\rho_H(xy)\le\rho_H(x)\rho_H(y)$, and $\rho_H(1)=1$, by applying the corresponding absolute-value inequalities at every maximal ideal. If $q(a)=0$ for a monic $q\in B[Z]$, then $\rho_A(a)\le\sigma_B(q)$: at each maximal ideal of $A$, put $v=|a|$ and $S=\sigma_B(q)$. Each coefficient has value at most $S^i$ by contraction of $\rho$. If $v>S$, every nonleading term has value at most $S^iv^{e-i}<v^e$, contradicting the strong triangle inequality in the residue field applied to $q(a)=0$. Take the supremum of $v$. This includes $S=0$.

source.place: Section 1.4, Proposition 5 and Lemma 13, reverse inequality; pointwise reconstruction avoiding division by a zero supremum

proof.text: Coefficient bounds multiply: if the coefficients at distance $i$ below the leading coefficient of monic $p$ and $q$ have $\rho$ at most $R^i$, then the coefficient at distance $k$ of $pq$ is $\sum_{i+j=k}p_iq_j$, with $p_0=q_0=1$. The inequalities of step 1 bound each summand by $R^{i+j}=R^k$ and hence bound the sum by $R^k$. Repetition gives the same bounds for any finite product and any positive power. For $R=0$ all the lower coefficients have seminorm zero, and the identical argument works, with $R^0=1$.

source.place: Section 1.4, Lemma 11, printed p.25: coefficient convolution argument

proof.text: First suppose $A$ is a domain. Choose a presentation $\pi:T_r\twoheadrightarrow B$ and put $I=\ker(\varphi\pi)$. It is proper because $A\ne0$. The lifted normalization gives $T=K\langle U_1,\ldots,U_d\rangle\to T_r\to B$ whose composite with $B\to B/\ker\varphi=T_r/I$ is injective and finite. Therefore $T\to A$ is injective and finite: if $u_j$ span $B/\ker\varphi$ over $T$ and $v_k$ span $A$ over $B$, the products $u_jv_k$ span $A$ over $T$, since the $B$-action factors through this quotient. A nonzero $t\in T$ has nonzero image in the domain $A$, so multiplication by it is injective. Thus $A$ is torsion-free over $T$.

source.place: Section 1.4, Lemma 13, first paragraph: normalize the image of B, using Section 1.2 Corollary 10

proof.text: Apply the maximal-fibre polynomial theorem to $T\hookrightarrow A$ and $a$. Write its polynomial as $p=Z^r+\sum t_iZ^{r-i}$. Every maximal ideal of $A$ contracts to a maximal ideal of $T$: its residue field is finite over $K$, so the image of $T$ in it is a finite-dimensional domain over $K$ and therefore a field (multiplication by a nonzero element is an injective, hence surjective, linear map). The nonempty fibres in that theorem therefore exhaust $\operatorname{Max}A$. Its fibre formula yields $\rho_A(a)=\max_i\rho_T(t_i)^{1/i}$. Explicitly, each fibre maximum is bounded by the latter maximum, giving one inequality. Conversely, $|t_i\bmod\mathfrak m|^{1/i}\le\rho_A(a)$ for every $\mathfrak m$ and $i$; raising to the integer $i$ and taking suprema gives $\rho_T(t_i)\le\rho_A(a)^i$, the other inequality.

source.place: Section 1.4, Lemma 12(ii)-(iii) and Lemma 13, domain case

proof.text: Let $b_i$ be the images of $t_i$ under the map $T\to B$ from step 3. Evaluation commutes with this coefficient map, so $q=Z^r+\sum b_iZ^{r-i}$ annihilates $a$. Contraction of the supremum seminorm gives $\sigma_B(q)\le\max_i\rho_T(t_i)^{1/i}=\rho_A(a)$. Step 1 gives the reverse inequality. This proves the domain case for an arbitrary finite map $B\to A$, including a map with kernel.

source.place: Section 1.4, Lemma 13, domain case: coefficient map through the original B

proof.text: For general $A$, choose a fresh presentation $T_h\twoheadrightarrow A$. Specialize the polynomial/affinoid comparison statement to $J=0$ in $h$ variables to obtain Noetherianity of $T_h$. Every ideal of its quotient $A$ is finitely generated: take finitely many generators of its inverse-image ideal in $T_h$ and map them to $A$. The minimal primes $\mathfrak p_1,\ldots,\mathfrak p_s$ of $A$ are consequently finite. Every prime contains a minimal prime. They are nonempty: otherwise there are no primes at all, and the radical/intersection theorem gives $1\in\sqrt{(0)}$, contrary to $A\ne0$. Each $A_j=A/\mathfrak p_j$ is a nonzero affinoid domain, and $B\to A_j$ is finite, using images of the original finite spanning set. Every maximal ideal of $A$ contains some $\mathfrak p_j$, and the maximal ideals of $A_j$ are exactly those containing $\mathfrak p_j$, with the same residue fields. Thus $R:=\rho_A(a)=\max_j\rho_{A_j}(a_j)$.

source.place: Section 1.4, Lemma 13, minimal-prime reduction; Stacks Tags 00FR and 00E0 (lemma-Noetherian-irreducible-components and lemma-Zariski-topology)

proof.text: Apply the domain argument of steps 3-5 to each $B\to A_j$, obtaining monic $q_j\in B[Z]$ of positive degree with $q_j(a_j)=0$ and $\sigma_B(q_j)=\rho_{A_j}(a_j)\le R$. Put $P=\prod_{j=1}^s q_j$. For each minimal prime $\mathfrak p_j$, the factor $q_j(a)$ belongs to $\mathfrak p_j$, so $P(a)$ belongs to all minimal primes. Every prime contains one of them, hence $P(a)$ lies in every prime. The radical/intersection theorem says precisely that $P(a)^N=0$ for some $N\ge1$. Set $Q=P^N$; then $Q(a)=0$ and $Q$ is monic of degree $N\sum_j\deg q_j\ge1$.

source.place: Section 1.4, Lemma 13, final paragraph, nilpotent-power argument; Stacks Tag 00E0 (lemma-Zariski-topology), parts (4),(7)

proof.text: Each lower coefficient at distance $i$ of every $q_j$ has $\rho_B$ at most $R^i$. Step 2 therefore gives this bound for $Q=P^N$, so $\sigma_B(Q)\le R$. Step 1 applied to $Q(a)=0$ gives $R\le\sigma_B(Q)$. Its lower coefficients and its positive degree give the required equation and equality. In particular when $R=0$ the argument uses no division and retains seminorm-zero coefficients.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NG-adecf096a (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the mathematics in full. There is no local copy of the Bosch source, so I downloaded the primary Bosch PDF (read only, kept in /tmp) and read Section 1.4 Lemmas 11-13, printed pp.25-28. The item statement is Lemma 13 and is unchanged and faithful. Steps 1-8 follow Bosch's proof. Step 1 is the root bound, done pointwise and including S=0. Step 2 is the Lemma 11 coefficient convolution. Step 3 is normalization of B/ker phi through I=ker(phi pi) and gives a finite torsion-free T inside the domain A. Step 4 applies the new node; maximal ideals contract to maximal ideals (a finite-dimensional K-domain is a field), and both inequalities between the suprema are given. Step 5 maps the coefficients into B, with contraction plus the step-1 reverse bound. Step 6 gets Noetherianity from the J=0 clause of the closed-point comparison node, finitely many nonempty minimal primes from the 00FR/00E0 leaves, and Max A as a union of the Max A/p_j. Steps 7-8 give a nilpotent product, then a power Q=P^N with positive degree and equality, including R=0. The new node lem-trf-tate-torsionfree-fibre-polynomial is exactly Bosch Lemma 12(i)-(ii), with C also assumed affinoid, which is harmless here. I checked it independently: T_d is factorial, so the minimal polynomial has coefficients in T and generates the kernel (unique because it is monic); lying-over and the root/coefficient formula give the fibre equality. I tested it on d=0, on C=T[eps]/(eps^2) with c=eps, and on c in T. It does not restate a clause of its parent, since the item needs normalization, coefficient transport and the nilpotent-power argument. Duplicate search with rg -L found no duplicate; candidates read: normalization-lift, supremum-calculus, spectral-banach-norm (reduced C, algebraically closed K), finite-extension-bounded-powers, tate-unit criterion, powerbounded-integral. No SGA, tool_uses is empty, and this is not a re-split note. No changes made.
